sentences.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption reviews election funding, spending and disclosure arrangements in NSW.
sentences.support: The Commission focused on four key areas of the election funding and electoral expenditure framework.

sentences.text: It consulted experts and regulators and compared NSW electoral rules with Australian and overseas systems.
sentences.support: The Commission also undertook its own extensive research into the electoral laws of NSW and analysed electoral regimes in other jurisdictions.

sentences.text: The Commission identifies excessive administrative demands, weak party accountability, limited sanctions and inadequate disclosure as weaknesses in the system.
sentences.support: the regulatory system emphasises administration rather than regulatory oversight and governance of political parties.

sentences.text: Its 22 recommendations address regulatory capacity, party governance, audits and penalties, public funding and more timely, accessible disclosures.
sentences.support: Transparency is to be enhanced by increasing timeliness, accessibility and intelligibility of disclosures.

findings.quote: Incomplete, delayed and difficult-to-access disclosure information impedes civil society’s ability to offer effective oversight over electoral funding arrangements.

notes: The summary includes all 22 recommendations. Proposed legal changes are described as recommendations rather than current requirements.
